subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Non-germ cell testicular tumors; epididymitis and orchitis
vignette: A 6-year-old boy presents with signs of precocious puberty, including facial hair and penile enlargement. Testicular ultrasound reveals a small, well-circumscribed mass. Orchiectomy shows a golden-brown tumor composed of cells with eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions (Reinke crystals).
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Leydig cell tumors are mostly benign sex cord stromal tumors that are golden brown and contain Reinke crystals (eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions). They produce androgens or estrogens, leading to precocious puberty or gynecomastia. Sex cord stromal tumors arise from embryonic sex cord derivatives and make up about 5% of testicular tumors.

explanation_incorrect.A: Sertoli cell tumors (androblastomas) are also mostly benign sex cord stromal tumors but are not characterized by Reinke crystals or golden-brown color.
explanation_incorrect.B: Yolk sac tumor is a malignant germ cell tumor with Schiller-Duval bodies and elevated AFP, occurring in young children but not with Reinke crystals or virilization.
explanation_incorrect.D: Primary testicular lymphoma is an aggressive tumor of males over 60, often bilateral, not a golden-brown crystal-containing tumor of a child.
explanation_incorrect.E: Seminoma is a germ cell tumor of young adults with fried egg cells and PLAP elevation, not Reinke crystals.

educationalObjective: Leydig cell tumor is a mostly benign golden-brown sex cord stromal tumor with Reinke crystals causing precocious puberty or gynecomastia.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Non-germ cell testicular tumors; epididymitis and orchitis
vignette: A 38-year-old man presents with a painless testicular nodule. Orchiectomy reveals a tumor arising from sex cord stroma. The pathologist notes it is histologically similar to Leydig cell tumors but lacks Reinke crystals and is mostly benign.
question: Which of the following is the correct term for this tumor?
explanation_correct: Sertoli cell tumor, also called androblastoma, arises from sex cord stroma and is mostly benign. Sex cord stromal tumors (which include Sertoli and Leydig cell tumors) make up about 5% of testicular tumors and are derived from embryonic sex cord derivatives that develop into Sertoli and Leydig cells of the seminiferous tubules.

explanation_incorrect.A: Seminoma is a germ cell tumor with fried egg histology and PLAP elevation, not a sex cord stromal tumor.
explanation_incorrect.B: Choriocarcinoma is a malignant germ cell tumor with trophoblastic elements and high hCG.
explanation_incorrect.C: Yolk sac tumor is a malignant germ cell tumor with Schiller-Duval bodies and high AFP.
explanation_incorrect.D: Leydig cell tumor also arises from sex cord stroma but is distinguished by golden-brown color and Reinke crystals, which are absent here.

educationalObjective: Sertoli cell tumor (androblastoma) is a mostly benign sex cord stromal tumor; sex cord stromal tumors are about 5% of testicular tumors.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Non-germ cell testicular tumors; epididymitis and orchitis
vignette: A 68-year-old man presents with painless enlargement of both testicles over several weeks. He has no fever or signs of infection. Orchiectomy shows a diffuse infiltrate of large lymphoid cells. Metastatic workup reveals involvement of other sites.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Primary testicular lymphoma is a malignant, aggressive tumor that is typically a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, often bilateral, and is the most common testicular cancer in males over 60 years old. Bilateral painless enlargement in an elderly man with a diffuse large lymphoid infiltrate fits this diagnosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Seminoma is the most common testicular tumor overall but occurs in young adults and is typically unilateral with fried egg cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Embryonal carcinoma is a painful hemorrhagic germ cell tumor of younger men, not an elderly man with bilateral disease.
explanation_incorrect.D: Leydig cell tumor is a small benign sex cord stromal tumor causing hormonal symptoms, not an aggressive bilateral lymphoma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Chronic orchitis is an inflammatory condition, not a malignant lymphoid infiltrate with metastatic spread.

educationalObjective: Primary testicular lymphoma is an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, often bilateral, and the most common testicular cancer in men over 60.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Non-germ cell testicular tumors; epididymitis and orchitis
vignette: A 21-year-old sexually active man presents with 3 days of left scrotal pain and tenderness localized to the posterior aspect of the testis, with mild swelling. Lifting the scrotum relieves the pain. He has no fever, and the cremasteric reflex is intact. Urinalysis shows leukocytes.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and its most likely causative organism?

options.text: Testicular torsion; caused by congenital bell clapper deformity
Varicocele; caused by increased venous pressure
Epididymitis; commonly caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae in young males
Hydrocele; caused by a patent processus vaginalis

explanation_correct: Epididymitis is inflammation of the epididymis, presenting with localized pain and tenderness over the posterior testis and a positive Prehn sign (pain relief with scrotal elevation). In young males the most common causes are Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae; in older males, Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas are associated with UTI and BPH. It may progress to involve the testis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Torsion has an absent cremasteric reflex, a negative Prehn sign, and acute severe pain, not the gradual posterior pain with relief on elevation described here.
explanation_incorrect.B: Mumps orchitis causes testicular pain and swelling with infertility risk, not posterior epididymal tenderness with a positive Prehn sign.
explanation_incorrect.C: Varicocele is a chronic painless bag of worms that enlarges with Valsalva, not an acute painful inflammation.
explanation_incorrect.E: A hydrocele is a painless transilluminating fluid collection, not a tender inflamed epididymis.

educationalObjective: Epididymitis causes posterior testicular pain with a positive Prehn sign; young males are infected by Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Non-germ cell testicular tumors; epididymitis and orchitis
vignette: An 18-year-old unvaccinated man develops painful swelling of both testicles 2 weeks after an episode of parotitis and fever. He is concerned about the possible long-term consequence of this infection on his fertility.
question: Which of the following best describes this condition and its major complication?

options.text: Mumps orchitis, which increases the risk of infertility; orchitis is rare in males under 10 years old
Epididymitis from Chlamydia trachomatis, which is treated with antibiotics
Leydig cell tumor causing precocious puberty
Yolk sac tumor with elevated AFP

explanation_correct: Orchitis is inflammation of the testis, presenting with testicular pain and swelling. Mumps orchitis increases the risk of infertility and is rare in males under 10 years old. This patient's preceding parotitis and unvaccinated status make mumps the likely cause.

explanation_incorrect.B: Chlamydial epididymitis causes posterior epididymal tenderness and a positive Prehn sign, not bilateral testicular swelling following parotitis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Torsion is acute, unilateral, and associated with an absent cremasteric reflex, not post-infectious bilateral testicular swelling.
explanation_incorrect.D: Leydig cell tumor is a benign sex cord stromal tumor with Reinke crystals and hormonal effects, not an infectious orchitis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Yolk sac tumor is a malignant germ cell tumor of young children with elevated AFP, not an infection following parotitis.

educationalObjective: Mumps orchitis causes painful testicular swelling, increases infertility risk, and is rare in males under 10.
